elements.quote: The purpose of the present study was to systematically review the current literature... This systematic review (PROSPERO: CRD42023395005) followed the preferred reporting items for systematic reviews and metaanalyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly identifies the report as a systematic review.

elements.quote: The purpose of the present study was to systematically review the current literature on the interventions taken through social media for promoting lay people's oral health.
elements.reason: The main objective is explicitly stated in the abstract.

elements.quote: Out of the 1934 records identified in the initial search, 10 studies met the inclusion criteria and were included in the qualitative synthesis.
elements.reason: The abstract mentions that studies met inclusion criteria but does not specify what the inclusion/exclusion criteria were.

elements.quote: A comprehensive search was conducted in four electronic databases (PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and Cochrane Library) for relevant articles published between 2012 and 2023.
elements.reason: Information sources are named, but the date each source was last searched is not reported (only a publication date range).

elements.quote: The quality of the studies included in the systematic review was evaluated by the quality assessment tools for intervention studies recommended by the National Collaborating Centre for Methods and Tools.
elements.reason: The abstract specifies the tool used to assess risk of bias/quality of included studies.

elements.quote: Data such as study design, sample size, follow-up duration, utilized social media platforms and main findings were extracted from the eligible studies... included in the qualitative synthesis.
elements.reason: The abstract describes data extraction and states results were synthesized qualitatively.

elements.quote: 10 studies met the inclusion criteria and were included in the qualitative synthesis. These studies comprised seven randomized control trials, one field trial and two quasi-experimental.
elements.reason: Number of studies and study designs are reported, but the total number of participants is not given in the abstract.

elements.quote: The implementation of social media interventions positively influenced multiple aspects of oral health among the laypeople.
elements.reason: Main outcomes are summarized only in general narrative terms, without numbers of studies/participants per outcome or specific effect details.

elements.quote: included in the qualitative synthesis
elements.reason: No meta-analysis was conducted (qualitative synthesis only), so no summary estimate applies.

elements.quote: The implementation of social media interventions positively influenced multiple aspects of oral health among the laypeople.
elements.reason: Several included studies compared groups, but the abstract does not indicate direction of effect or which group was favored for any comparison.

elements.quote: The quality assessment categorized 30% of the studies as 'strong', 50% as 'moderate', and the remaining as 'weak'.
elements.reason: Although quality ratings are reported, the abstract does not summarize limitations of the evidence (e.g., risk of bias, inconsistency, imprecision) as limitations.

elements.quote: Online platforms such as YouTube, WhatsApp, Instagram, and Telegram can be effectively utilized to promote oral health among patients.
elements.reason: The abstract provides a general interpretation and implication of the results.

elements.quote: This study was funded by Research Affairs of Dental School, Shahid Beheshti University of Medical Sciences.
elements.reason: The funding source for the review is stated in the abstract-section text.

elements.quote: This systematic review (PROSPERO: CRD42023395005)
elements.reason: The abstract provides both the register name (PROSPERO) and the registration number.

elements.quote: While there have been several studies investigating the impact of social media on dentistry, there is limited information available on the effectiveness of online interventions through social media aimed at preventing diseases and promoting oral health among laypeople.
elements.reason: The Introduction describes the current state of knowledge (existing studies on social media in dentistry) and explicitly identifies the uncertainty/gap (limited information on effectiveness of online interventions for oral health).

elements.quote: Clinicians can benefit from familiarizing themselves with the interventions described in the literature and evaluating the reported outcomes. This will enable them to make informed decisions using the cost-effective and accessible tool of social media. Therefore, the objective of this study is to systematically review the current evidence regarding social media-based interventions designed for disease prevention and oral health promotion among laypeople.
elements.reason: The importance and need for the review are explained (informing clinicians' decisions with a cost-effective tool) and the review objective is stated.

No similar prior systematic reviews are mentioned or cited in the retrieved evidence; the Introduction frames the topic as having limited information, so no update/replication justification is required.

elements.quote: Social media is able to increase the degree of knowledge in people of all ages, and it can be used as a promising clinical tool for the prevention and promotion of oral health
elements.reason: A brief mechanism is hinted at (social media increases knowledge and provides accessible health information), but a clear mechanism of action for the intervention is not fully described.

No logic model or hypothesised relationships between intervention components and outcomes is reported, and the retrieved evidence does not indicate the review addresses complex interventions requiring one.

elements.quote: This systematic review aims to address the following PIO question: 'What is the effect of social media on prevention and promotion of oral health compared with conventional strategies among lay people of any age without disability or systematic diseases?'
elements.reason: The review objective/question is explicitly stated as a PIO-formulated question, with P, I, and O components defined in the same section.

elements.quote: The focus is on (I) social media-based interventions that employ a group approach for information dissemination. The desired outcomes include (O) any changes in oral health status, knowledge, beliefs, and attitudes resulting from social media interventions.
elements.reason: The planned comparison is stated within the PIO question ('compared with conventional strategies'), an appropriate PICO variant for this review of intervention effects.

elements.quote: The review encompasses (P) laypeople from diverse backgrounds, including different age groups, genders, socioeconomic statuses, ethnicities without any disability or systematic diseases. The focus is on (I) social media-based interventions that employ a group approach for information dissemination. The desired outcomes include (O) any changes in oral health status, knowledge, beliefs, and attitudes resulting from social media interventions. This includes short and long-term effects, regardless of the duration of follow-up. The full-text articles from 2012 to 2023 focus on randomized controlled trials (RCTs), quasi-randomized trials and field trials were included
elements.reason: Population, intervention, outcomes, follow-up, and eligible study designs are all specified in the Eligibility Criteria section.

elements.quote: The full-text articles from 2012 to 2023 ... were included in the current study. ... were published in languages other than English were excluded. The conference proceedings, editorials, commentaries, review articles, pilot studies ... were excluded.
elements.reason: Publication year range, English-language restriction, and publication/report status (excluding conference proceedings, editorials, commentaries, reviews, pilot studies) are specified.
No evidence distinguishes exclusion because outcomes were not measured from exclusion because outcome results were not reported.

elements.quote: Eight studies employed a design in which two or more groups were compared [14-21], and the rest reported changes before and after the intervention within a single study group [22, 23].
elements.reason: Study groupings (comparative vs single-group pre-post) and platforms are described, but the synthesis groups are not explicitly linked to the comparisons defined in the review objectives (social media vs conventional strategies).
Restrictions (e.g., English-only, exclusion of people with disability/systematic diseases) are stated but no rationales are provided for these restrictions.

elements.quote: The search was performed from 1st January 2012 until 25 th Augst 2023
elements.reason: A search period is reported, but it is ambiguous whether this is the coverage date range of publications or the date the search was last run; a specific 'last searched' date is not clearly stated.

elements.quote: Four electronic databases, including PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and Cochrane Library, were searched thoroughly.
elements.reason: Database names are reported, but no search platforms/interfaces or database coverage dates are specified.
No registers, regulatory databases, or online repositories were reported as searched (PROSPERO was only a registration, not a study source).
No websites or search engines were reported as searched.
No organisations or manufacturers were reported as contacted to identify studies.
No individuals were reported as contacted to identify studies.

elements.reason: The types of reference lists examined are specified: reference lists of included studies and previously published reviews.
No backward or forward citation searching was reported.
No journals or conference proceedings were consulted directly as sources.

elements.quote: following search queries were designed: ('social media' OR 'social network * ' OR ... OR 'oral cancer'). ... elements.quote: The search was performed from 1st January 2012 until 25 th Augst 2023, seeking papers published in English language. The search was limited to the title and abstract in PubMed and Embase...
elements.reason: Date, language, and field limits are described, but no justification linking these limits to the eligibility criteria is provided.

elements.reason: Two researchers are named for full-text evaluation and quality rating, but the number of reviewers who performed the data extraction itself is not explicitly stated.

elements.quote: two trained researchers (Fz.F and F.F) conducted the screening process independently

elements.quote: Six studies assessed the objective oral health using gingival index [17, 19], modified gingival index [15], decayed, missing, and filled teeth (DMFT) [21], bleeding index [15], plaque index [15-17], number of decayed teeth [17, 18, 21], community periodontal index [16], and white spots [17]. Behavioral changes, including dental cleaning behavior [16, 19, 21, 22], perceived self-efficacy, perceived benefits/barriers, motivational beliefs [19], and psychosocial variables [16], were assessed in different studies. Dental anxiety [14], knowledge [14, 20, 22] and attitude about oral health [22] were other measured outcomes.
elements.reason: Outcomes are listed (objective oral health measures, behavioral changes, dental anxiety, knowledge, attitude) but they are reported as outcomes measured in included studies rather than prospectively defined outcome domains for which data were sought, and definitions are not provided.
No time frame of measurement for each outcome domain is specified in the methods; only follow-up durations appear in Table 1 for individual studies.
The manuscript does not state whether all compatible results within each outcome domain were sought.
No process for selecting which results to collect is described.
No changes to outcome-domain inclusion, definitions, or importance are reported.
No changes to result-selection processes are reported.
No prioritisation of key outcomes for interpreting conclusions with rationale is reported.

elements.quote: For each selected article, data such as study design, sample size, follow-up duration, utilized social media platforms and main findings were extracted.
elements.reason: The Methods list several extracted variables (study design, sample size, follow-up duration, social media platforms, main findings), but the list is not exhaustive or defined; Table 1 shows additional variables (aim, country, outcomes, participant characteristics) that are not declared as sought data items in the Methods.
No statement describing assumptions made about missing or unclear study information during data extraction is present in the retrieved evidence.
No citation of a tool or guidance used to determine which data items to collect is reported; only PRISMA adherence and PROSPERO registration are mentioned.

elements.quote: The quality of the studies included in the systematic review was evaluated using the 'quality assessment tools for quantitative studies', recommended by the National Collaborating Centre for Methods and Tools [12].
elements.reason: The risk-of-bias/quality assessment tool is explicitly named with its source.

elements.quote: The evaluation covered domains including selection bias, study design, confounding factors, blinding, data collection methods, the integrity of the intervention, method of analysis, withdrawal and dropout.
elements.reason: The domains assessed by the tool are listed.

elements.quote: The overall quality of each study was categorized as 'weak', 'moderate', and 'strong'. Studies devoid of any 'weak' rating and receiving at least four 'strong' ratings were considered 'strong'.
elements.reason: Overall judgement categories and the rules for deriving them are reported.
No evidence of adaptations to an existing tool; an existing standard tool with its dictionary was used as-is.
No newly developed tool was used; an existing published tool was applied.

elements.quote: Fz.F and F.F read and rated the full texts, and in case of disagreement, M.N made the final decision.
elements.reason: Two reviewers rated studies independently and a third reviewer resolved disagreements.
No evidence that authors sought or confirmed risk-of-bias information from study investigators; no such process is reported.
No automation tools are reported as used in the risk-of-bias assessment.

No effect measure (e.g., risk ratio, mean difference) is specified for any outcome. The review reports a qualitative synthesis only, and neither the Methods nor Results sections state any effect measures used for the outcomes listed (e.g., gingival index, DMFT, knowledge).

elements.quote: 10 articles that met the inclusion/exclusion criteria were included in the qualitative synthesis (Fig 1).
elements.reason: The review conducted a qualitative synthesis with no meta-analysis; no effect sizes were synthesized, so interpretation thresholds for effect sizes do not apply.

elements.quote: 10 articles that met the inclusion/exclusion criteria were included in the qualitative synthesis (Fig 1).
elements.reason: No quantitative synthesis was performed, so there was no need to re-express synthesized results using another effect measure.

elements.quote: 10 articles that met the inclusion/exclusion criteria were included in the qualitative synthesis (Fig 1).
elements.reason: Since no effect measures were used in a qualitative-only synthesis, no justification of effect measure choice was required.

elements.quote: In the first stage the titles and abstracts of the remaining studies were screened against the inclusion and exclusion criteria. Those that were relevant and met the inclusion criteria were flagged for a full-text review in the second stage of the selection process... Subsequently, full texts of the potentially relevant articles were thoroughly evaluated by two researchers (Fz.F and F. F). In case of any disagreement, the final decision was made after consulting a third person (Z. G).
elements.reason: The manuscript describes the process for deciding study eligibility (two-stage title/abstract and full-text screening against inclusion/exclusion criteria, with dual independent review and third-party adjudication). The review conducted a single qualitative synthesis, so this process applies to that synthesis; no separate synthesis groupings requiring tabulation against planned groups are reported.

The retrieved evidence describes data extraction items (study design, sample size, follow-up duration, platforms, main findings) but no methods for preparing data for presentation or synthesis, such as handling of missing summary statistics or data conversions, are reported anywhere in the Methods or elsewhere.

elements.quote: An overview of the included studies, containing their characteristics, study designs, follow-up durations, and other relevant information, can be found in Table 1.
elements.reason: Tables 1 and 2 are referenced with some indication of their content (study characteristics; quality assessment domains), but the Methods section does not explicitly describe tabulation methods or the full data included in the tables.

No methods for graphical display of results are described. The only figure is the PRISMA flow diagram of study selection (text_9/figure_4), which is not a display of study results or syntheses, and no graphs of results are reported.
No basis for ordering or grouping studies within tables or graphs is reported anywhere in the retrieved evidence.
No non-standard graphs are used or reported, so no rationale for such graphs is required.
No meta-analysis or statistical synthesis was performed, so no software/packages were used or needed.

elements.quote: 10 articles that met the inclusion/exclusion criteria were included in the qualitative synthesis (Fig 1).
elements.reason: A qualitative (narrative) synthesis is mentioned as the alternative to meta-analysis, but the Methods do not describe or justify how the synthesis of results was actually conducted; the only justification for not meta-analysing appears in the Discussion.
No meta-analysis was performed, so no model or rationale applies.
No meta-analysis was performed, so no statistical method applies.

elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly identifies that meta-analysis was not possible and reports the reasons (heterogeneity in designs, populations, outcomes, and interventions), although this is reported in the Discussion rather than Methods.
No methods to explore causes of heterogeneity among study results are reported anywhere in the retrieved evidence; the review conducted only a qualitative synthesis of 10 studies.

elements.quote: 10 articles that met the inclusion/exclusion criteria were included in the qualitative synthesis
elements.reason: No meta-analysis was performed (qualitative synthesis only), so subgroup analysis or meta-regression factors and levels do not apply.

elements.quote: 10 articles that met the inclusion/exclusion criteria were included in the qualitative synthesis
elements.reason: Without meta-analysis or subgroup/meta-regression analyses, reporting of study-level vs within-study contrasts does not apply.

elements.quote: 10 articles that met the inclusion/exclusion criteria were included in the qualitative synthesis
elements.reason: No subgroup comparisons within a meta-analysis were conducted, so methods for comparing subgroup effects do not apply.
Although meta-analysis was unsuitable and a narrative approach was used, no informal heterogeneity-exploration methods (factors and levels) are described in the retrieved evidence.
No heterogeneity analyses (pre-specified or otherwise) are reported, so there is nothing to identify as not pre-specified.
No sensitivity analyses are described anywhere in the retrieved evidence; the review reports only a qualitative synthesis and quality assessment, with no mention of sensitivity analyses.
Since no sensitivity analyses are reported at all, there is no identification of any analysis as pre-specified or not pre-specified.

The manuscript describes a general quality assessment (National Collaborating Centre for Methods and Tools tool covering selection bias, confounding, blinding, etc.), but no methods for assessing risk of bias due to missing results (reporting biases) are reported anywhere in the retrieved evidence.
No existing reporting-bias assessment tool was used, so there are no domains/items or overall judgement process for such a tool to report.
No adaptations to an existing reporting-bias tool are described or implied; no reporting-bias tool was used at all.
No newly developed reporting-bias tool is mentioned in the retrieved evidence.

Although reviewer numbers and disagreement resolution are reported for the general quality assessment (text_8: 'Fz.F and F.F read and rated the full texts, and in case of disagreement, M.N made the final decision.'), no such procedures are reported for an assessment of risk of bias due to missing results, which was not performed.
No reporting-bias assessment was conducted, so no processes for obtaining or confirming information from study investigators apply.
No automation tools for reporting-bias assessment are mentioned in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: The quality of the studies included in the systematic review was evaluated using the 'quality assessment tools for quantitative studies', recommended by the National Collaborating Centre for Methods and Tools [12].
elements.reason: A named tool is reported, but it is a study-level quality appraisal tool (EPHPP-style), not a certainty/confidence-in-body-of-evidence system (e.g., GRADE); no certainty assessment of outcomes is described.

elements.quote: The evaluation covered domains including selection bias, study design, confounding factors, blinding, data collection methods, the integrity of the intervention, method of analysis, withdrawal and dropout.
elements.reason: The domains/factors considered by the assessment tool are explicitly listed, with a dictionary providing criteria (S1 File).

elements.quote: Studies devoid of any 'weak' rating and receiving at least four 'strong' ratings were considered 'strong'. Studies with one 'weak' rating and three or less 'strong' ratings were qualified as 'moderate', while studies with two or more 'weak' ratings were regarded as 'weak' ones.
elements.reason: Explicit decision rules for deriving overall ratings ('weak', 'moderate', 'strong') and their interpretation are provided.
No review-specific certainty thresholds or rationales beyond the generic tool rules are reported.
No adaptations to the assessment tool are described; the tool is reported as used with its standard dictionary.

elements.quote: Fz.F and F.F read and rated the full texts, and in case of disagreement, M.N made the final decision.
elements.reason: Two independent raters and a third-reviewer disagreement-resolution procedure are reported.
No processes for obtaining or confirming information from investigators are described.
No automation tools supporting certainty/quality assessment are mentioned.
No methods for reporting certainty of the body of evidence (e.g., Summary of Findings tables or GRADE profiles) are described; only a study-level quality table (Table 2) is presented.
No standard phrases incorporating certainty or source guidance for their interpretation are reported.

elements.quote: After conducting the electronic search, a total of 1,934 records were identified. Following the removal of duplicates, 1342 papers remained. Through title and abstract screening, 64 studies were identified as potentially relevant
elements.reason: Numbers identified (1934), removed before screening (duplicates), screened (1342), and excluded at screening (implied by 64 remaining; flow diagram figure_4 shows n=933 unrelated and other exclusion counts) are all reported.

elements.quote: Upon full-text assessment, 54 studies were ... excluded, and 10 articles that met the inclusion/exclusion criteria were included
elements.reason: 64 full texts assessed for eligibility and 54 excluded; the flow diagram (figure_4, chunk text_9) provides primary reasons for exclusion (e.g., not interventional n=42, intervention not social media n=8, full article not found n=2, pilot study n=2).

elements.quote: 10 articles that met the inclusion/exclusion criteria were included in the qualitative synthesis (Fig 1)
elements.reason: Number of included studies (10) is reported in text and in the flow diagram (figure_4: 'Studies included in qualitative synthesis (n=10)').
No ongoing studies or associated reports are mentioned anywhere in the retrieved evidence; nothing indicates ongoing studies exist.
There is no evidence this review is an update of a previous review; it is registered as a new PROSPERO review, so update reporting does not apply.
Screening was performed manually by two reviewers (text_7); no automation tools were used, so distinguishing human vs automated exclusions does not apply.

elements.quote: Upon full-text assessment, 54 studies were ... excluded, and 10 articles that met the inclusion/exclusion criteria were included in the qualitative synthesis (Fig 1).
elements.reason: The PRISMA flow diagram (Fig 1, chunk text_9, visible in figure_4) lists categories of excluded full-text reports with counts and reasons (e.g., 'Not interventional (n=42)', 'The intervention was not defined as using social media (n=8)', 'Pilot study (n=2)'), and title/abstract exclusion reasons. However, no individual excluded studies are cited/referenced with study-specific explanations, which the item requires.
elements.note: Visual evidence: figure_4 (parent chunk text_9) shows the flow diagram with exclusion reason boxes and counts.

elements.quote: Regarding the study design, seven RCTs [14-20], a field trial [21] and two quasi-experimental studies [22, 23] were included in this systematic review.
elements.reason: All 10 included studies are cited via reference numbers in the Study Characteristics section and are individually listed by author in Table 1 (tables_0-2).

elements.quote: Table 1. Summary of included studies in systematic review. | Author (Year, country) | Study type | Aim | sample size/ Participants | Follow up | Social media | Outcomes | Main findings
elements.reason: Table 1 presents characteristics (author, year, country, design, aim, sample, follow-up, platform, outcomes, findings) for all 10 studies, supporting comparison.
